profile.headline: Fullstack Software Engineer | JavaScript, Python, HTML, CSS, React, PostgreSQL, Node, RPA, AWS, GitHub
profile.summary:
I am...

• A disciple of Jesus Christ, serving Him in a variety of ways in my life
• A husband who strives to be the best I can be for my wife
• A full stack software engineer (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node, Express, React, Redux, Python, Flask)
• A researcher (of just about anything that catches my attention)
• A writer (of both fiction and non-fiction)
• A Forex trader

I desire to be...

• Better at all the above things I already am
• Improving in all areas of my life
• Learning and growing, always

My personal Bible study has led to four core principles I try to live by:

• Treat others as I would want to be treated (Mt 22:39; Jam 2:8)
• When others fail to do right, to remember mercy, for I am just a sinner too (Lk 6:36; Rom 3:23)
• Do all for the use of edifying others toward a closer relation to God (Rom 14:19)
• Reflect God in all I do, for that is what He designed every person to do (Gen 1:26-27) and saved me to do (Eph 2:8-10; 1 Pet 1:16)

positions.title: Bot Curator II (Full-stack Software Engineer)
positions.description:
A Bot Curator II is senior software engineering role with oversight of our software bots performing Robotic Process Automation (RPA), saving our clients money and freeing their human "grunt" data entry labor to be used in other needed areas.

Responsibilities include:
1. Oversee bot health (monitoring Sentry status, AWS logs)
2. Fix bugs that are detected by us or the clients in bot operations
3. Meet with clients over video meetings as needed for bot discussions
4. Write up client change orders for bot enhancements
5. Code bot changes for change order requests
6. Support Bot Engineers in areas unfamiliar to them for bot design and bug fixes
7. Monitor security status for codebase
8. Work with other bot curators help solve more challenging issues and foster a group learning
9. Help junior curators to perform in their roles

Contributed to company by:
1. Instrumental in foundational design decisions and continued review support for the company's first fully productized bot (Reggie - an Ebilling bot: https://simplefractal.com/products/reggie/)
2. Drove and implemented the separation of an overly large mono-repo into various smaller repositories to help overcome size limitations that the mono-repo was causing with bot deploys.
3. Stepped into a lead role over a team designing a new bot due to the original lead leaving the company: guided junior developers for initial coding, then finalized bot personally.
4. Leveraging AI to enhance coding productivity while not giving up control of code development.

positions.title: Bot Curator
positions.description: This was a brand new position at this time, with my selection as the initial (and originally only) Bot Curator. The company needed to split out the maintenance of currently operational bots from the Bot Engineer responsibilities to free them up for new bot designs.

positions.title: Junior Bot Engineer
positions.description:
Rapidly progressed in understanding RPA processes, specifically:
1. The primary stack for our bots (Node.js) 
2. AWS lambda and step functions
3. Postgres databases

Contributed to company by:
1. Taking initiative in DRYing up code
2. Taking initiative in enhancing code flexibility and usability for database interfacing
3. Individually producing a new bot from specs

positions.title: Associate Pastor
positions.description: Primary duties include teaching adult Bible study courses Sunday mornings, leading a men's Bible study, occasional visitation and preaching as well.

positions.title: Graduate Faculty
positions.description: The "2nd" of my two duties I did at Piedmont was part-time teaching at the graduate level the Research: Writing and Communication course.  This was a remote, online, contract position.

positions.title: Graduate Academic Advising and Registrar Assistant
positions.description: The "1st" of my two duties at Piedmont was advising MABS and PhD students about course selections and other academic matters in fulfilling degree requirements. This was a remote, online, contract position.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant and Adjunct Teacher
positions.description: My earliest position at Piedmont, prior to earning my Ph.D., involved certain teaching and advising duties. Primarily each term I assisted the Dean of the School of Bible and Theology in setting up for and grading of beginning Greek tests and quizzes, and quizzes for the Ph.D. Greek courses (during which I also created a way of automating test grading in the student system of the Greek tests). During Fall 2012, I also had the opportunity to be the Teaching Assistant for the E4-12 Introduction to Hermeneutics Class, and Fall 2013 was an adjunct teacher for Bible Doctrines I. This was an on-site job.

positions.title: Website Designer
positions.description: Primarily using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, my duties involved designing the look and feel (user interface) of the PCC site (and related family of sites), leveraging the high quality graphics that the print marketing group did to have the sites stand out.

positions.title: Motor Coach Designer/Draftsman
positions.description: Using AutoDesk's Mechanical Desktop software, I designed 3D models and 2D prints of Class A motor coaches. My primary duties were dealing with the special orders and accommodating those customer requests for smooth integration into the production line. (NOTE: from about Aug 2005-2007 was a minor role as a remote worker to update certain Excel files).
